source.title: NCCP Classification Document for SACT Induced Nausea and Vomiting, V6 (2025)
source.mapping_rule: For combination SACT, use the most emetogenic active component. Multi-day and multi-phase regimens require day/phase-specific selection.
source.antiemetic_link_note: All user facing antiemetic links use national NCCP guidance. Medical oncology regimens open the NCCP Medical Oncology document and haemato oncology regimens open the NCCP Haemato Oncology document. Existing emetogenic classifications and traffic light mappings are unchanged.
source.medical_oncology_antiemetic_guidance_tit: NCCP Supportive Care Antiemetic Medicines for inclusion in NCIS (Medical Oncology)
source.haemato_oncology_antiemetic_guidance_tit: NCCP Supportive Care Antiemetic Medicines for Inclusion in NCIS (Haemato-Oncology)
source.evidence_overlay: Current NCCP V8 2025 antiemetic medicines remain the Irish default. MASCC/ESMO 2023 evidence is shown as a transparent overlay where it differs (notably steroid-sparing in most MEC and selected enhanced MEC prophylaxis).
source.cuh_reference_note: CUH 2021/2024 supportive-medicine sheets are retained as local reference material. Their adjunct medicines are separated from national CINV prophylaxis and require current pharmacy/local-policy review.

generic-high-cuh-v2-05-21.label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for high emetogenic risk
generic-high-cuh-v2-05-21.summary: Legacy compatible internal mapping retained for backward compatibility. User facing supportive care now opens national NCCP antiemetic guidance for the active oncology context.
generic-high-cuh-v2-05-21.subsequent_days: Follow the current NCCP guidance for high emetogenic risk and reconcile with the active regimen and local policy.

generic-moderate-cuh.label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for moderate emetogenic risk
generic-moderate-cuh.summary: Legacy compatible internal mapping retained for backward compatibility. User facing supportive care now opens national NCCP antiemetic guidance for the active oncology context.
generic-moderate-cuh.subsequent_days: Follow the current NCCP guidance for moderate emetogenic risk and reconcile with the active regimen and local policy.

generic-low-cuh-v2-05-21.label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for low emetogenic risk
generic-low-cuh-v2-05-21.summary: Legacy compatible internal mapping retained for backward compatibility. User facing supportive care now opens national NCCP antiemetic guidance for the active oncology context.
generic-low-cuh-v2-05-21.subsequent_days: Follow the current NCCP guidance for low emetogenic risk and individual clinical requirements.

nccp-parenteral-high.label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for high emetogenic risk
nccp-parenteral-high.summary: NCCP V6 class recommendation: NK1 antagonist + 5-HT3 antagonist + corticosteroid + olanzapine, adjusted for the active regimen, interactions and local policy.
nccp-parenteral-high.subsequent_days: Use the NCCP V6 high-risk subsequent-day schedule; anthracycline/cyclophosphamide and immune-checkpoint contexts require regimen-specific steroid review.

nccp-parenteral-moderate.label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for moderate emetogenic risk
nccp-parenteral-moderate.summary: NCCP V6 class recommendation: 5-HT3 antagonist + corticosteroid, adjusted for the active regimen, interactions and local policy.
nccp-parenteral-moderate.subsequent_days: Consider the NCCP V6 subsequent-day corticosteroid schedule where appropriate; account for steroids already included in the SACT regimen.

nccp-parenteral-low.label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for low emetogenic risk
nccp-parenteral-low.summary: NCCP V6 class recommendation: one 5-HT3 antagonist or corticosteroid before treatment, selected according to the regimen and local policy.
nccp-parenteral-low.subsequent_days: No routine subsequent-day prophylaxis in the class table unless clinically indicated.

nccp-minimal-no-routine-prophylaxis.label: NCCP antiemetic guidance
nccp-minimal-no-routine-prophylaxis.summary: NCCP V6: no routine antiemetic prophylaxis required; treat symptoms and individual risk factors according to local policy.

nccp-oral-moderate-high.label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
nccp-oral-moderate-high.summary: NCCP V6 Table 5: daily oral 5-HT3 antagonist prophylaxis, selected and reviewed under local policy; avoid routine prolonged steroids for continuously administered oral therapy.
nccp-oral-moderate-high.subsequent_days: Continue daily while the oral SACT risk persists, with review for interactions and adverse effects.

nccp-oral-minimal-low.label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
nccp-oral-minimal-low.summary: NCCP V6 Table 5: antiemetics on an as-required basis; select an appropriate agent under local policy and account for interactions/QT risk.
nccp-oral-minimal-low.subsequent_days: Continue only as required and reassess persistent symptoms.

docetaxel-cuh-v2.label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for low emetogenic risk
docetaxel-cuh-v2.summary: Use the national NCCP antiemetic guidance for emetogenic support. Confirm docetaxel specific steroid premedication and other supportive medicines against the current regimen protocol and applicable local policy.
docetaxel-cuh-v2.subsequent_days: Follow the current NCCP antiemetic guidance and the regimen specific steroid schedule in the current protocol.

nccp-v8-ac-v08417.label: NCCP V8 antiemetic guidance — reviewed regimen/phase
nccp-v8-ac-v08417.summary: NCCP V8 Medical Oncology Table 1, anthracycline/cyclophosphamide row: NK1 antagonist, 5-HT3 antagonist, dexamethasone on Day 1 and olanzapine. Use the regimen-specific supportive-care draft for doses and pharmacy review.
nccp-v8-ac-v08417.subsequent_days: The dedicated AC row continues aprepitant on Days 2–3 and olanzapine on Days 2–4, with no routine dexamethasone on Days 2–4. Reconcile breakthrough treatment and avoid unintended duplicate steroids.

nccp-v8-docetaxel-moderate-v08417.label: NCCP V8 antiemetic guidance — reviewed regimen/phase
nccp-v8-docetaxel-moderate-v08417.summary: NCCP V8 moderate emetogenic-risk guidance applies. Reconcile the antiemetic steroid with the docetaxel premedication course; do not add two separate dexamethasone prescriptions.
nccp-v8-docetaxel-moderate-v08417.subsequent_days: Follow the prescribed docetaxel steroid schedule and the reviewed regimen-specific draft. Confirm subsequent antiemetics and patient-specific risks with oncology pharmacy.

nccp-v8-paclitaxel-v08417.label: NCCP V8 antiemetic guidance — reviewed regimen/phase
nccp-v8-paclitaxel-v08417.summary: Low emetogenic risk during the paclitaxel phase. Use the separate taxane supportive-care draft, including the protocol hypersensitivity premedication; do not carry the AC antiemetic course into this phase.
nccp-v8-paclitaxel-v08417.subsequent_days: No routine multi-day AC antiemetic course. Adjust for symptoms and the current NCCP guidance/local policy.

nccp-v8-trastuzumab-v08417.label: NCCP V8 antiemetic guidance — reviewed regimen/phase
nccp-v8-trastuzumab-v08417.summary: Trastuzumab-only continuation has minimal emetogenic risk. No routine chemotherapy antiemetic course; manage previous infusion reactions or symptoms individually.
nccp-v8-trastuzumab-v08417.subsequent_days: No routine AC or taxane antiemetic course during trastuzumab-only continuation.

nccp-v8-moderate-v08418.label: NCCP V8 antiemetic guidance — reviewed treatment day
nccp-v8-moderate-v08418.summary: NCCP V8 Table 1 moderate risk row. Use the exact treatment-day supportive-care draft; reconcile medicines, renal/hepatic function and individual risk.
nccp-v8-moderate-v08418.subsequent_days: Moderate risk: dexamethasone on the two days after each administered chemotherapy dose, with rescue treatment as prescribed.

nccp-v8-low-v08418.label: NCCP V8 antiemetic guidance — reviewed treatment day
nccp-v8-low-v08418.summary: NCCP V8 Table 1 low risk row. Use the exact treatment-day supportive-care draft; reconcile medicines, renal/hepatic function and individual risk.
nccp-v8-low-v08418.subsequent_days: No routine subsequent-day prophylaxis; rescue treatment as prescribed.

nccp-oral-vinorelbine-v08420.label: NCCP oral vinorelbine support · reviewed weekly plan
nccp-oral-vinorelbine-v08420.summary: NCCP Table 5: one 5-HT3 antagonist—ondansetron 8–16 mg totaldaily OR granisetron 1–2 mg totaldaily.
nccp-oral-vinorelbine-v08420.subsequent_days: Table 5 says continue daily; for once-weekly vinorelbine the prescriber must state the number of days. Do not automatically turn this into indefinite daily treatment or import an IV moderate steroid/NK 1 schedule.

nccp-v8-carboplatin-v08420.label: NCCP V8 dedicated carboplatin AUC ≥4 antiemetic plan
nccp-v8-carboplatin-v08420.summary: Day 1: aprepitant 125 mg, ondansetron 16 mg and dexamethasone 12 mg orally. Dedicated carboplatin row; no routine olanzapine.
nccp-v8-carboplatin-v08420.subsequent_days: Days 2–3 aprepitant 80 mg daily; Days 2–4 dexamethasone 8 mg daily. NCIS lists metoclopramide 10 mg three times daily on subsequent days without an end day or PRN qualifier: prescriber/pharmacy must specify duration and suitability.

breakthrough.summary: Reassess emetogenic risk, disease/medication causes and adherence; add an antiemetic from a different mechanism and use it regularly rather than PRN while breakthrough symptoms persist.
breakthrough.warning: Agent choice, dose, QT risk, sedation, extrapyramidal effects and drug interactions require clinical/pharmacy review.
